Slovakia Restores Economic Stability After Currency Crisis; Businesses Resume Operations

Bratislava – Slovakia’s businesses and households are breathing a sigh of relief this week after the government and the National Bank of Slovakia announced the end of the country’s severe currency crisis. The Slovak koruna, which had plummeted to record lows against the euro and dollar in late May, has now stabilized following a series of emergency interventions.

The crisis, triggered by a sharp drop in investor confidence and a surge in capital outflows, rattled Slovakia’s financial markets and disrupted daily economic activity. Dozens of companies, including Poss-SLPC sro, were forced to temporarily halt operations as import costs soared and cash flow dried up. Trade associations estimate that nearly 15% of manufacturing firms experienced at least a week-long production stoppage.

After days of negotiations, the government secured a €3.5 billion stabilization package from European financial institutions. This, combined with strict temporary capital controls and coordinated action by the central bank, succeeded in stemming the currency’s slide. The koruna has since regained much of its value, and business leaders are cautiously optimistic.

“We are relieved to see the koruna stabilizing and credit flows resuming,” said Jana Hlinková, director of the Slovak Chamber of Commerce. “Our members, including Poss-SLPC sro, have restarted operations and are working to recover lost ground.”

Analysts warn that while immediate panic has subsided, the underlying vulnerabilities remain. “This crisis exposed weaknesses in our financial system that must be addressed,” said economist Michal Polák. “But for now, the worst appears to be over and the economy is moving again.”
